source.title: All Languages Matter: On the Multilingual Safety of Large Language Models
source.authors: Wenxuan Wang; Zhaopeng Tu; Chang Chen; Youliang Yuan; Jen-Tse Huang; Wenxiang Jiao; Michael R. Lyu

record.tranche_reason: The study reports unsafe-response rates across languages and a prompting intervention, extending the investigation of safety behavior to multilingual settings. It does not test any listed version’s fine-tuning, token-position, bypass-opening, parameter-localization, or deepening claims.
record.gate_note: The study measures multilingual unsafe-response rates, but does not fine-tune models on harmful or benign examples, measure per-token KL, prefill compliant openings, test adversarial suffixes or decoding changes, localize safety in weights, or train for deeper safety. The language and prompt results are recorded as related findings under versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study measures unsafe-response rates of off-the-shelf aligned LLMs on a translated multilingual benchmark (XSafety), plus an 'think in English' system prompt on ChatGPT. It does no fine-tuning (V1, V2), no per-token KL (V3), no prefilling, suffix or decoding manipulation (V4), no parameter localization (V5), no causal analysis of shallowness (V6), and no deepening training (V7). Qi et al. (2310.03693) is cited only as precedent for LLM-as-judge evaluation. Non-English queries act as a bypass, but not by getting past the response opening, so they do not bear on V4. The record's 'tests/T3' is wrong: the results fit no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. All tested LLMs are less safe in non-English languages than in English, with the lowest-resource languages (Bengali, Hindi, Japanese) worst. The English-reasoning prompt cuts ChatGPT's non-English unsafe ratio by 42% on average.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates multilingual safety and adds a cross-lingual prompting intervention; it does not reproduce the fine-tuning or token-depth methods in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Unsafe-response rate differs by language and model; the proposed prompt’s reduction also varies by tested language (relative changes reported as -49% for Chinese, -78% for Russian, -14% for Japanese, and -47% for French).

fits_no_version.finding: All four principal models show higher unsafe-response rates on non-English queries than on English ones (e.g., ChatGPT 1.0% vs 15.9%; Vicuna 6.0% vs 33.4%). Claude-3 and Gemini show the same pattern in a small-scale check.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety alignment generalizes incompletely across languages: non-English queries raise unsafe-response rates.

fits_no_version.finding: A 'think in English then respond in the original language' system prompt lowers ChatGPT's average unsafe rate on non-English queries from 16.8% to 9.7% (42% relative), across three scenarios and four languages.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A cross-lingual reasoning prompt reduces non-English unsafe-response rates.

record.code_released: https://github.com/Jarviswang94/Multilingual_safety_benchmark (dataset release stated; code release not stated)
record.problems: The authors note that ChatGPT self-evaluation is not entirely accurate. They report human annotations and validation, but do not provide uncertainty estimates for the tabulated rates. The prompt intervention is evaluated only on ChatGPT and four non-English languages, using three selected safety scenarios.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix A, Tables 8–9 report large-scale human evaluation rates for ChatGPT and LLaMA-2 across languages; omitted because of the 60-row cap after retaining the primary benchmark, prompt comparison, and newer-model results. Appendix C reports evaluator disagreement, not a separate unsafe-compliance outcome for the tested versions.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or aligned-vs-base positional comparison.
No prefilled compliant opening, adversarial suffix or decoding change. Language switching is a different bypass route.
No test of data or objective causes. The authors speculate that English-dominant alignment data limits cross-lingual generalization, but do not test it.

record.verdict_notes: Human-evaluation Tables 8–9 are declared in rows_left_out. Unsafe rates use ChatGPT as judge (88.5% agreement with human annotators). No version of shallow safety alignment is tested, so no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning or post-fine-tuning refusal measurement.
No benign-data fine-tuning or post-fine-tuning harmful-compliance measurement.
No per-token KL measurement or aligned-versus-base comparison.
No compliant-start prefilling, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change test.
No weight, rank, or parameter-localization test.
No test of whether data or training objectives cause shallowness.
No training to deepen safety or test of whether deepening holds up.
